blocks.text: DOC’s architecture linked centrally held spatial data with operational databases and field workflows. Continued development had to support both specialist GIS users and staff using the browser applications.

blocks.text: The 2003 releases established browser access for distributed offices. Maintaining that access meant supporting older computers and slow connections alongside the specialist workstations.

blocks.text: Departmental teams included Science and Technology & Information Services Division, Information Management Unit and Spatial Information Management at Head Office, alongside conservancy information-management units. Duane Wilkins recalls that Eagle Technology designed DOCgis before 2003, with departmental analysts and developers continuing its development. He also recalls difficult relations between regional teams and the GIS manager. Around a decade later, Wilkins returned to lead GIS; in 2012 the team became a shared service for the regions, a change he remembers as highly successful.

blocks.text: DOC publicly described DOCgis as part of an organisation-wide national GIS on 24 August 2009. A DOCgis map print dated 12 February 2013, later reproduced in official New Zealand Conservation Authority papers, shows DOCgis still in use.
